author: kingpanther13
releaseNotes:
v4.4.8 - 2026-10-03
- build(deps): bump the gradle-dependencies group with 2 updates ([#488](https://github.com/kingpanther13/Hubitat-local-MCP-server/pull/488), @app/dependabot)
- ci: replace E2E watchdog v2 with v3 (manual admin, package deployment, wedge reboot) (#485)
- ci: stop linting, parsing and testing the retired v1/v2 watchdogs (#493)
- fix: keep durable state off the request path and cut device and e2e overhead (#494)
  - Faster MCP requests: the server no longer reads stored app state on every request.
  - Device tools respond faster, especially `hub_list_devices` on large hubs and when listing only device ids and labels.

v4.4.7 - 2026-09-29
- fix: DateTime hub variables, live rule locals, numeric device ids, post-update setup refresh, RM edit guards (#480)
  - DateTime hub variables keep their time, and rule-local listings show current values.
  - Device attribute reads and event history accept numeric device IDs.
  - The server refreshes subscriptions and schedules after a code update and retries incomplete setup.
  - Clearer errors for malformed settings, missing files, and unsupported trigger edits.
  - Self-update protection recognizes the server's Apps Code ID.
- docs: generate TOOL_GUIDE.md from the served tool guide (#481)
- fix: hub_get_info appUpdate derives updateAvailable from versions (#474) (#475)
  - The MCP Rule Server no longer reports an app update as available when you're already on the latest version — both in `hub_get_info` and the app's "Update available" banner. The check is derived from the versions themselves, so an upgrade clears the prompt immediately; a `checkInProgress` flag marks that the GitHub check runs asynchronously.

v4.4.6 - 2026-09-27
- fix: native-app device pickers, sub-pages and UI page checks; Room Lighting create (#477)
  - Room Lighting and other built-in apps: device selections copied from an app's configuration can be written back directly, and motion/illuminance settings on the app's sub-pages can now be set.
  - The AI can now create new Room Lighting instances. Asking for one on a hub that does not have the Room Lighting app adds it first, the same as Apps > Add Built-In App.
  - Edits that the Hubitat app page would refuse (for example a required field left empty) are now refused with the fields named, instead of saving an incomplete app.
  - Fields you never set are saved with their default values (fixes Room Lighting showing "rise above null").
  - Rule Machine: a rule create with an invalid trigger or action no longer leaves an empty rule behind, and invalid time or periodic schedule settings are rejected with a clear message.

v4.4.5 - 2026-09-26
- feat: per-device and per-variable Hub Mesh link/share (#448) (#462)
  - Manage Hub Mesh device and variable sharing from MCP:
    - Link a device or hub variable that a peer hub shares, and unlink it again (local only — the peer's original is never touched).
    - Share or unshare a hub variable over Hub Mesh.
    - Clear guidance when a link doesn't take (the peer is still reconnecting — wait and retry) and when unsharing would leave stale copies on other hubs.

v4.4.4 - 2026-09-26
- fix: refused addAction editor cleanup, modern-era check, setVariable numOp, patches trigger/action ops (#471)
  - Rule Machine: a rejected action add (unknown source variable, filtered device attribute, bad math operand, bad runCommand parameter) no longer leaves the Rule Machine action editor open with stale fields — the next action is created clean, and an editor that could not be closed is reported instead of hidden.
  - Rule Machine: setVariable / setLocalVariable now support `numOp: "add number"` with `value` to add to the variable instead of setting it; unsupported operations are rejected loudly instead of being silently converted to a plain set.
  - Rule Machine: `patches` now accepts `removeTrigger`, `modifyTrigger`, and `modifyAction`, so a trigger can be retargeted (remove + add) in one call.
  - MCP protocol: future protocol revisions newer than 2026-07-28 will be handled as modern-era instead of falling back to legacy behavior.

v4.4.3 - 2026-09-25
- fix: hub_report_issue reports the real hub model; make bug-report error retention opt-in (#468)
  - Bug reports generated by the server now show the hub's real hardware model (e.g. "C-8 Pro") instead of an internal id.
  - Keeping recent errors for bug reports is now an opt-in advanced setting (off by default), which removes an app-state write from every logged error.
  - `hub_call_rule` with `action=actions` runs a rule's actions through Rule Machine's own Run Actions button, so it keeps working when the hub's load limiter is blocking RMUtils.

v4.4.2 - 2026-09-25
- fix: resolve verified issue 407 findings (#465)
  - Improve paused-rule feedback and avoid rejecting redundant device authorization when inventory is temporarily incomplete.
  - Keep recent server errors available for issue reports even after native logs roll over.
  - Apply a safe minimum to enabled request budgets and clarify backup recovery advice.
- fix: hub_get_info reports the real hardware model, not the internal hardwareID (#466) (#467)
  - `hub_get_info` now reports the hub's real hardware model (e.g. "C-7", "C-8 Pro") instead of an internal id. The raw internal id remains available under a new `platformHardwareId` field.
- feat: add protected-app controls for generic app mutations (#456)
  - Choose Protected apps in the MCP server settings to prevent generic MCP tools from editing, disabling, deleting, or operating those installed apps.
  - The MCP server protects its own instance by default after installation or upgrade. You can change the selection in the Hubitat UI; dedicated Developer Mode maintenance remains available.

v4.4.1 - 2026-09-23
- fix: keep producedBy/triggered provenance in device event history (#459)
  - Device event history now shows what caused each event: the app, rule, or device that produced it (`producedBy`) and the apps it triggered (`triggered`), plus the event type. Filter by `command-on` / `command-off` to see which rule or app sent a command.

v4.4.0 - 2026-09-23
- feat: add hub-level Hub Mesh tools (hub_get_hub_mesh, hub_update_hub_mesh) (#438)
  - New: Hub Mesh tools — read which peer hubs your hub is meshed with (`hub_get_hub_mesh`: enabled state, peer hubs, shared/linked devices and hub variables, sync interval, mode-following hub) and change hub-level Hub Mesh settings (`hub_update_hub_mesh`: enable/disable, full-sync interval, follow a peer hub's modes, store a peer hub's mesh token)
